## Summary

Render artifact integrations through the accepted, provider-neutral chat UI.

- Promote integrated artifacts/references into individual pills while keeping unmatched entries grouped without duplicate pills.
- Show the input-width details context view with a linked title, bounded description, tabbed state lists, and applicable actions.
- Add collapsed-by-default **Autopilot** and **Activities**, remembered selections, enabled-rule counts, paged activity counts, and wheel handoff at list boundaries.
- Render action-request snapshots and automation notices through shared chat-card primitives.
- Preserve keyboard navigation, focus across refreshes, accessible content/help, safe markdown rendering, and themed component fixtures.

This is the existing agreed UI/UX packaged as its own review layer, not a new visual redesign. The upstream adaptation also preserves the original exclusion of promoted integrations from grouped fallback pills.

## Stack

This is **3 of 4**, based on #343001.

| Order | PR | Base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | #343002 - Shared integration runtime | `main` |
| 2 | #343001 - Agent host, extension API, and agent tools | #343002 |
| 3 | **#343003 - Generic artifact UI (this PR)** | #343001 |
| 4 | #343000 - GitHub pull request integration | #343003 |

Part of the replacement stack for #337678 and #338107. This layer has no dependency on the new GitHub provider.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` - **passed** without the GitHub layer.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` - **passed**.
- `git --no-pager diff --name-only HEAD -- '*.ts' | xargs ./node_modules/.bin/eslint --quiet` - **passed**, run before committing this slice; edited regressions were rechecked afterward.
- `git --no-pager diff --name-only HEAD -- '*.css' | xargs npm run stylelint --` - **passed**, all 10 CSS files.
- `git diff --cached --check` - **passed** before committing.
- UI, keyboard, focus, scrolling, and accessibility tests - **353 passed**:

No new live Code OSS/manual screenshot run was performed for this restack. Existing themed fixtures are included, and the behavior above was validated with DOM tests.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call, cold-session loop, provider delegation, IPC protocol request, per-registration match loop, and absence of a shared concurrency limiter are all directly traced. Exact session artifact counts and provider match duration vary, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: IPC requests plus integration-provider match and model-initialization work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On each cold session ownership change, cost grows with every recorded artifact having a link or URI; each artifact acquisition then iterates every registered integration, so provider matching scales as artifacts × integrations, while all artifact acquisitions are launched concurrently without a shared limiter.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive IPC/provider work and contention during session activation, increasing session-open latency and reducing extension-host or remote-agent throughput.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The toolbar previously built grouped artifact/reference pill data without acquiring an artifact integration model for each record, so opening a session generated no per-artifact integration subscriptions or provider-match sweep.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new autorun loops over all session artifacts and immediately calls acquireArtifactIntegration for every linked/URI record, retaining successes for the session but starting all cold acquisitions in one burst.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 614 invokes `_sessionsManagementService.acquireArtifactIntegration(current, artifact.id)` from the newly added loop over the complete session artifact collection; before this hunk the toolbar performed no such per-artifact acquisition.
Findings.Title: Bound integration discovery instead of acquiring every artifact at once
Findings.Impact: Opening an artifact-heavy agent session (for example one recording many files, links, images, and commits) now sends one acquisition per record; remote acquisition is an IPC subscription, and local model initialization invokes every registered integration's asynchronous match for each record. This background burst competes with opening and using the chat even when the user never opens an artifact pill.
Findings.Evidence: The changed loop accepts every artifact with link or URI and invokes acquireArtifactIntegration. That service delegates to the provider; AgentHostArtifactIntegrations.acquireArtifact calls access.acquireArtifact (and can additionally acquire the local fallback), ArtifactIntegrationClient sends a distinct `acquire` transport request per call, and ArtifactModel.initialize/refresh iterates all registry integrations whose ArtifactBinding.initialize calls each integration's async `match`. The toolbar test uses four records and the implementation acquires all four before any integration contribution is known. Successful models are cached only by the new lifetime map; failures are removed and can be retried after subsequent session-change events.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve integrated-pill behavior but put discovery behind a shared bounded queue (prioritizing visible records) and avoid re-running no-match work until the artifact or integration-registry revision changes; if possible, batch candidate discovery per session rather than opening one subscription per artifact.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The collapsed state, synchronous constructor path, item cap, unbounded detail-section multiplicity, and virtualized-row disposal/recreation are directly traced. The exact frame cost depends on snapshot size and viewport history density, reflected in medium severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: WorkbenchList instances, DOM nodes, event listeners, item arrays, and synchronous layout work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For every currently rendered artifact-action request row, construction scales with every captured detail section and up to 200 items per section; the details-array count is not capped, and virtualizing then re-rendering a row recreates this work.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher chat-history render/scroll latency plus avoidable CPU, allocation, and GC pressure, with potential dropped frames when several automation requests are visible.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Artifact-integration requests previously fell through the system-initiated request renderer to the lightweight notification/text presentation; they did not construct structured detail sections or WorkbenchList widgets.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new specialized request part starts collapsed but its constructor still loops through the complete snapshot, creates a WorkbenchList for every nonempty detail section, splices all items, and lays each list out before the user expands the card.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 128 synchronously instantiates a `WorkbenchList` inside the constructor's loop over snapshot details, despite the shared card having already initialized itself as collapsed.
Findings.Title: Build artifact action detail lists only after expansion
Findings.Impact: Recurring automatic artifact actions can place several compact collapsed cards in one viewport (the fixture exercises three). Merely opening or scrolling the chat now constructs all hidden detail list infrastructure; each section may carry 200 validated items even though CSS hides the entire body until disclosure.
Findings.Evidence: ChatActionRequestContentPart calls `setExpanded(false)` during construction. ChatArtifactActionContentPart then iterates every `presentation.details`; line 128 instantiates WorkbenchList, line 139 inserts the full item array, and line 141 performs layout immediately. Validation caps each detail at 200 items but does not cap the number of details. ChatListRenderer owns the part in `elementDisposables`, which are cleared when a row is virtualized, so revisiting the row rebuilds it.
Findings.Recommendation: Render only the header initially and create the details DOM/list widgets on first expansion; retain them while that row remains rendered, and dispose them with the row as today. Keep accessible text generated from the snapshot so accessibility does not require eager visual widgets.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The fan-out, key-level deduplication, test-observed count, protocol boundary, and panel-click reachability are directly established. Provider-side duration is variable, so the finding remains medium severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Artifact-details IPC subscriptions and provider detail models
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One panel open starts one acquisition for every distinct `(integrationId, detailsId)` referenced by all contributions' main, sections, and lists; cardinality is deduplicated by that key but is otherwise unbounded by validation, and all requests begin concurrently.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive IPC/provider work and contention when opening artifact details, delaying the main visible details and increasing remote/local provider load.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no artifact details context panel on this path and therefore no set of detail subscriptions opened from a pill click.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Constructing ArtifactDetailsModel gathers every main/section/list details ID and creates an ArtifactDetailsLease for all of them immediately, even though the panel initially displays only the main details and one selected list.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 106 creates a new `ArtifactDetailsLease` for each entry in the full `wanted` map; each new lease immediately starts `acquireDetails`, placing all tabs/sections onto the click path.
Findings.Title: Acquire only the detail section needed for the initial panel
Findings.Impact: A single click on an integrated pill opens all tab and section subscriptions at once. The added tests demonstrate three acquisitions for the normal main/checks/comments panel and six when another provider contributes details; remote models map each lease to a separate `details` transport request, so providers with more lists amplify click latency and service load.
Findings.Evidence: Lines 95-98 add every main, section, and list details ID to `wanted`; line 106 constructs a lease for every key, and the lease constructor immediately calls `presentation.model.acquireDetails`. ArtifactIntegrationClient.acquireDetails sends an individual protocol request/subscription, while provider detail models are retained until panel disposal. The test `main click opens full details` asserts `acquired: ['main', 'checks', 'comments']`, proving inactive details are fetched on the initial click rather than selection.
Findings.Recommendation: Initially lease the main details plus the explicitly requested/selected section, then acquire an inactive tab's details when it is selected (retaining loaded leases for the open panel). Queue any remaining prefetch with a small shared limit rather than starting every subscription together.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch to an agent session whose input toolbar shows recorded artifacts and references
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The grouped pills can render before discovery completes, so acquisition is not a hard prerequisite for chat use; however, promoted integrated pills depend on the acquisitions, and the burst competes with session activation on the extension host/agent connection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire a live artifact integration subscription/model
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per linked/URI artifact on a cold session; remote access emits one `acquire` request per artifact, with an optional second local-fallback acquisition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-artifact integration acquisitions were initiated by SessionArtifacts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not a strict blocker for base chat rendering, but integrated-pill promotion waits for it and the aggregate burst contends with session startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Integration-defined asynchronous resource matching and possible resource creation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One `match` per registered integration for each newly acquired artifact model; resource creation is pooled only after a match.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This provider matching was not reached from toolbar construction for every session artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs behind each acquisition and can occupy provider/extension resources while the session opens.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Every session artifact with a link or URI after ID deduplication; each acquired artifact model checks every registered integration, so provider matching scales with artifacts × integrations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All per-artifact acquire promises are launched from one synchronous loop without a shared limiter. Each model checks registrations sequentially, but different artifacts run concurrently; AgentHostArtifactIntegrations may also acquire host and local fallback models for one artifact.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful and no-contribution models are retained for the current session/artifact lifetime, so warm reads avoid reacquisition. Changing session ownership clears all entries. Failed acquisitions are removed and can be retried after later session-change events. Retained models refresh against registry changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff loop, provider delegation, IPC request, registration sweep, cache lifetime, and lack of a shared limiter are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Artifact counts, integration counts, and match latency vary by session and installed extensions; sessions recording many files/links make the multiplicative burst realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: the PR newly fans discovery across the entire artifact collection with unbounded aggregate concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an integrated artifact's details panel and switch among state-list sections
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The main details subscription is needed for the authoritative title/description. Inactive list/section subscriptions are not needed for the initial visible selection, but are started on the same click and contend with the main request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per distinct details key; tests establish three on a normal main/checks/comments click and six with a second contribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No artifact-details panel or detail subscriptions existed on this pill-click path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The main request is critical; inactive requests are unnecessary for initial progress but contend with it and provider resources.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct `(integrationId, detailsId)` keys across all contributions' main, sections, and lists; shared IDs are deduplicated, but section/list counts are not capped.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Every missing key creates a lease whose async acquisition starts immediately; no panel-level limiter serializes or bounds these detail requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A detail model is shared by provider binding/details ID while references exist and leases are retained while the panel stays open. Closing the panel releases them, so reopening reacquires all details. Failures are shown and a later authentication recovery reacquires them.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: lease creation, immediate acquire call, protocol request, key deduplication, and test-observed counts are direct.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical built-in examples have three details keys, while extension-provided contributions can expose more and remote/provider latency varies.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: one click eagerly fans out to every inactive details source rather than loading the initial selection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or scroll a chat transcript containing automatic/manual artifact action requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Rendering each visible request row is synchronous on the UI path. The card header is all that is visible initially, but complete hidden detail sections and lists are constructed before the row can finish rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Currently rendered artifact-request rows × captured detail sections × items per section. Each detail is capped at 200 items, while the detail-section count is uncapped; compact collapsed cards allow several rows in one viewport.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Work is synchronous and serialized on the renderer/UI thread. Chat row virtualization bounds simultaneously retained rows, but disposal clears the parts and revisiting a row recreates them.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No lazy visual cache exists before expansion. A rendered row retains its widgets until virtualized; once disposed, re-rendering rebuilds all hidden lists. The persisted snapshot itself is already available and needs no boundary call.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the card is explicitly collapsed first, followed by synchronous per-section WorkbenchList creation, full splice, and layout; virtualization disposal is directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most snapshots are small, but recurring automation can produce multiple cards and providers may include several 200-item sections; exact WorkbenchList construction/layout duration is environment-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: hidden visual details are eagerly built on the transcript render/scroll path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand Activities, page older runs, reveal an activity, or change Autopilot configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Activities performs history I/O only after explicit expansion or paging. Reveal waits for chat opening and model readiness by user request. Autopilot configure/invoke calls occur only after a user action and are awaited for operation state, not during initial panel construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch one page of artifact run history
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call on first Activities expansion, then one per explicit Earlier Activities action; 50 runs per page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The UI had no Activities paging path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks only the expanded Activities content, not initial panel opening while collapsed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Configure, invoke, cancel, or reconcile an artifact action
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per explicit user operation; group configuration batches multiple rule values into one request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These controls were not present in this UI layer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Expected operation-specific wait after user intent; not on session startup or collapsed-panel rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open a target chat and wait up to 10 seconds for its request row when revealing an activity
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One open per explicit activity reveal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly required by the user-requested reveal and cancelled if the active session changes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: History pages are fixed at 50 runs and paging is user-driven; loaded pages are deduplicated by run ID. Configuration groups batch changed rule values into one configure call.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The Activities model has one `loading` guard and generation check, so normal page requests are serialized; replace-after-operation intentionally supersedes a pending generation. Autopilot suppresses duplicate pending rule/group operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Loaded activity pages remain for the panel-model lifetime; first-page loading is lazy, retries are explicit, and closing details drops the model. Configuration state comes from the live snapshot rather than a shadow cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: lazy trigger points, loading/pending guards, page size, and boundary calls are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider and chat-open latency vary, but multiplicity is bounded by explicit interactions and page size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression: these expensive operations are lazy, user-triggered, and reasonably serialized/batched.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full changed-file inventory. Reported three introduced regressions: cold-session integration acquisition fan-out, eager all-section detail subscriptions, and eager hidden list construction in collapsed chat cards. Paging, action operations, layout scheduling, disposal, and cache lifetimes were traced and did not yield further high-confidence findings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
